statement: Across three supervised direct-wired PCM captures, output 0x86 sends four wire bytes: stop group 2/5, configure group 2/5 mode 0. The Pixel client receives input 0x44 configuration status 0x20 for internal IDs 1/0 and status 0x10 for pad IDs 4/3; successful USB writes do not establish configuration acceptance. Its output 0x88 is 64 wire bytes, byte 1 length 30, with 30 meaningful bytes in each 31-byte slot; both unused slot bytes were zero throughout these captures. The iczero client instead sends output 0x87 selector 0/4: 1290 full 64-byte writes and two short 12-byte final writes, completing successfully. Input 0x44 is six bytes, IDs 0/1/3/4, status values 0x01/02/04/08/10/20 observed, trailing 3 bytes zero. Source labels suggest overrun/stopped/low/high/rejection/acceptance; no one-ACK-per-write or native FIFO-capacity/watermark rule is established. All observed output submissions completed status 0 with no pending writes; explicit final group 2/5 stops completed.
